title: Release choreography DSL + adaptive safety policy kit for traffic control
creator: Lina Chen
description: Goal: ship a compact, composable policy kit and small DSL that operators can attach to model routes to express staged-release choreography. The kit combines: 1) traffic-split expressions (time or metric-driven), 2) step-schedules with warmup/plateau/backoff phases, 3) probe definitions for shadow traffic and canary probing, and 4) guardrails that auto-throttle or auto-rollback based on multi-signal regressions (latency P95, error spike, end-to-end QA eval score). This ticket covers: DSL design, runtime policy evaluator, telemetry windows and aggregation rules, and a lightweight simulation harness for team validation.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can declare a rollout using the DSL with <= 8 lines that define traffic split, steps, and guardrails
Runtime enforces guardrails: if latency P95 crosses threshold for two consecutive windows rollout auto-pauses and alerts
Shadow probe capability: 1% of traffic can be mirrored with configurable sampling and response verification without impacting production path
Auto-rollback policy executes a safe rollback path (previous pinned model) when combined quality regressions detected by the scoring adaptor
Simulation harness produces deterministic replay and shows decisions for three representative scenarios: stable, transient spike, and quality regression
tasks: Design DSL grammar and example recipes (Miguel, Lina)
Implement policy evaluator in runtime (Rust) with pluggable telemetry adapters (ENG runtime team)
Add telemetry window aggregator and percentile calculator to metrics pipeline
Build simulation harness that can replay real request traces and emit decision timelines

decision_log: Use a tiny, JSON-first DSL (not YAML) to make parsing deterministic and safe in runtime
Guardrails operate on combined signals: latency, error rate, and quality delta. A policy triggers only when at least two signals exceed configured thresholds to reduce false positives
Minimum-stabilization-time will default to 120s to avoid reacting to micro-bursts; configurable per rollout
Shadow probes are asynchronous and responses are validated by a pluggable verifier so production path latency is unaffected
tradeoffs: Compact DSL reduces expressiveness vs. full policy language but simplifies safety reasoning and verification
Using combined-signal thresholds reduces sensitivity to single noisy metric but may delay detection of true regressions
Mirroring adds CPU/network cost; we limit default mirror to 0.5% to balance signal vs. cost
Simulation harness increases confidence but requires maintaining a replay dataset; decided to seed with 10k requests for initial rollout
